```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Path to first revenue: A is a one-sided subscription. A single podcaster paying the anchored ~$15-20/mo counts as a paying customer. B's dominant model is seller-pays-at-close, so revenue depends on a deal actually closing within 90 days. That requires buyer liquidity, which the brief shows is the documented failure mode.",
    "B's strongest sourced evidence argues against it. The closest comparable (DealMyApp) reports 500+ daily visitors and 30 listings but slow buyer conversion. The only sourced paid-acquisition test ($750 Indie Hackers sponsorship) produced 124 clicks and zero sales.",
    "Pricing headroom: B already has three 0% or near-0% commission rivals among its five listed competitors, which compresses the fee B can charge. A also faces free tiers (RSS.com), but its sourced price points of $19 to $199/mo at Transistor and Captivate show podcasters do pay recurring fees.",
    "Demand evidence: A's Reddit quotes come from paying users who complain about price yet say they pay for time-saving tools, which signals willingness to pay. B's demand quotes are one frustrated seller and one competing operator, and neither shows anyone paying.",
    "Build risk and the 90-day window: A's core features (upload, RSS, distribution, analytics) rest on open standards and existing infrastructure. Its ops burden is real but does not block getting a first customer. B needs legal setup before money can move, including a licensed escrow vendor and a state-by-state broker-licensing check."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's Case For claims a solo founder with AI agents could replicate Acquire.com's human 'acquisition expert' services at near-zero marginal cost. Its only citation is Acquire's pricing page, which shows that those services exist, not that agents can replicate them or that sellers would pay for an AI version. No test, comparable, or user quote supports it. The supporting claim that the build is feasible in weeks relies on DealMyApp, the same comparable that shows weak buyer conversion.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has real weaknesses. Its organic Reddit channel has no cost estimate and counts as missing. It says 'at least seven' competitors but lists five. The 'race to the bottom' comment has no URL. Gross margin after storage, bandwidth, and CDN costs is unknown. Neither brief shows a converted customer. A wins mainly because a one-sided subscription with sourced price points has a clearer path to one paying customer in 90 days than a cold-start two-sided marketplace that is paid only at close. The pick does not rest on strong positive evidence for A."
}
```
